question: What carrier, SIM, or mobile-network compatibility issues do Moto G7 users describe?
contexts: I checked the IMEI #s on each carrier's website (they have Moto G7 listed as a compatible device) and it comes back as incompatible on every carrier I've tried (even the ones that allow you to purchase Moto G 7 on their site i.e. mint mobile). The customer service reps also checked the IMEI #s for the phone I just purchased and said that the device is not compatible with their networks. Save yourself the trouble and buy the US Unlocked version of the Moto G7 Power. Roughly the same exact phone, a few more $ and is compatible with the carriers listed in the title/descriptions. I tried Cricket wireless, Mint Mobile and also T-mobile directly for anyone curious. I hope this helps save someone the time and frustration.

The battery is good at 3000MAH. The 1080p screen is brighter than my old Moto G6. The G7 is also unlocked and works on all four major US carriers AT&t Verizon Sprint and T-Mobile. So that means it will also work on all of their NVNO network carriers like Cricket, Metro by T-Mobile, Boost Mobile, Total wireless, Straight Talk, Google fi who uses Sprint's T-Mobile and US Cellular networks, and so many more. You name a carrier in the US and this Moto G7 will work on it. I am currently using my Moto G7 on Google fi. I can get the Sprint and T-Mobile networks in my area and the G7 switches automatically between them to find the best connection. My Moto G6 did not do that I had to force switch it. The G7 also as Wi-Fi calling. The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.

Poor cell service connectivity. This "international" edition of the Moto G7 comes with a great price but limited utility in my experience using AT&T and T-Mobile service. Connectivity is poor compared with the "domestic" version of the phone and WiFi calling is not available to use as a backup. The money saved is not worth it.
Moto g7 is good working phone. Moto g7 works great, no problems so far!

My Moto G2 never had a network connection issue. I want to like this phone as it has many nice features especially when considering the price point but this lack of network connectivity is going to force me to look elsewhere for a more reliable phone with regards to the ability to make and receive actual phone calls. Financially I hate to take a hit like that but I really need a phone that can reliably operate as a phone.

I loved the phone but could not get a signal when I was at home unless I went outside in the yard and I could NOT get the WiFi Calling feature to work so I returned it. Finally I bought the Moto G7 with the US warranty. It works perfectly with my Mint Mobile sim card. The Moto G7 Power has a slightly bigger screen and a much larger battery. Unfortunately the US version of the Moto G7 Power only comes in 32GB. So I sacrificed the larger battery for additional storage with Moto G7 64GB. So the moral of the story is do not buy the international version if you live in the USA!

Incompatible with T-Mobile - proof included - Moto G7 Plus (International version). See the screenshot for proof. This seems to be a great phone with one HUGE problem: it is not fully compatible with US carriers (T-Mobile in particular). Some of the calls will go directly to voicemail after long silence, and there is nothing you can do. For the calls that DO get through, network type instantly changes from LTE to 3G or even "H" (which is 2G) for the duration of the call. Bottom line: this is the international version, and it cannot reliably receive phone calls in the US. Huge disappointment. I will try a Moto G7 (not Plus, US version) and see if it is any better.

Moto g7. The Moto g7 is a decent phone with consistent performance and quality. To increase the speed go to Settings, Accessibility, Remove animations, Turn On. Warning! Be careful the Moto g7 International models are different and are not intended for the United States. International models are missing some 4G bands for the five networks (AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, US Cellular, and Verizon) in the United States.

Moto G7 plus does not work well. Bought this when it first came out right from Amazon. Moved T-mobile sim card from old phone Receives calls and makes calls but only in the US The following issues were not experienced by my family who are on the same family plan as I am and also was not experienced with my sim card in other phones. The issues are specific to the Moto G7+ I bought from this seller. text messages are delayed (both sending and receiving) When out of the US no service at all on this phone

Connectivity issues, no WiFi.. Phone was good for everything except WiFi connectivity. It refused to stay connected to WiFi and was constantly searching/scanning for a new connection. Which resulted in none of the apps working. Like Alexa, Amazon shopping, etc. Constantly loading or blank screen with network error. None of my other devices had an issue so it wasn't my router. When I began researching, this is a known problem with all g7 phones, even play and power versions. Even if you turned off the scanning feature. This was under a full us warranty and Motorola costumer support was terrible. They offered to send me a used test phone as a replacement. I declined. It's a shame because it was a nice phone for all the other things.
answer:
One reviewer reported that the Moto G7's IMEI came back as incompatible on every carrier they tried, including Cricket Wireless, Mint Mobile, and T-Mobile directly, and that customer service reps confirmed the device was not compatible with their networks. [d14d79450f3f_1]
Another reviewer stated that the unlocked Moto G7 works on all four major US carriers (AT&T, Verizon, Sprint, and T-Mobile) and their MVNO networks, and that they were using it on Google Fi with automatic switching between Sprint and T-Mobile. [14bf44a88dca_1]
A reviewer of the international edition described poor cell service connectivity on AT&T and T-Mobile compared with the domestic version, with no Wi-Fi calling available as a backup. [7cc9d91d904a_0]
One reviewer said they could not get a signal at home unless they went outside and could not get Wi-Fi Calling to work, then bought the US-warranty Moto G7, which worked perfectly with their Mint Mobile SIM. [9e96ef2d1bca_1]
A reviewer of the Moto G7 Plus international version reported it was not fully compatible with US carriers, particularly T-Mobile, with some calls going straight to voicemail and network type dropping from LTE to 3G or 2G during calls. [5d7f8b77d7f4_0]
Another reviewer warned that international models are missing some 4G bands for the five US networks (AT&T, Sprint, T-Mobile, US Cellular, and Verizon). [51b846eef7c6_0]
